atoms.text: This guide configures the FlowGate load balancer to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs every five minutes. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the FlowGate log delivery service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named FlowGateLogDeliveryRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal flowgate.example.com to perform AssumeRole. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::acme-lb-logs/lb-logs/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::acme-lb-logs. Leave the bucket policy of acme-lb-logs untouched, because it does not need to reference the role or the service. In the load balancer settings, set the log destination to acme-lb-logs with the prefix lb-logs/ and enter the ARN of the role. At each interval FlowGate assumes the role, receives temporary credentials, and writes gzip-compressed objects under lb-logs/YYYY/MM/DD/. Each object holds one line per request, containing the timestamp, client address, backend address, status code, and byte counts. To verify the setup, wait one delivery interval and list the prefix, where the first object should appear within ten minutes.

This guide configures the FlowGate load balancer to deliver access logs to the bucket acme-lb-logs every five minutes. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the FlowGate service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-lb-logs whose Principal is the service principal flowgate.example.com. Set the statement to allow PutObject on arn:example:storage:::acme-lb-logs/lb-logs/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::acme-lb-logs. Do not create any role or identity-based policy for this integration, because the bucket policy alone carries every permission. In the load balancer settings, set the log destination to acme-lb-logs with the prefix lb-logs/ and leave the role field empty. At each interval FlowGate authenticates as its service principal and writes gzip-compressed objects under lb-logs/YYYY/MM/DD/. Each object holds one line per request, containing the timestamp, client address, backend address, status code, and byte counts. To verify the setup, wait one delivery interval and list the prefix, where the first object should appear within ten minutes.

This guide enables EdgeStream to write hourly edge request logs for a content distribution into the bucket cdn-edge-archive. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the EdgeStream delivery service assumes, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named EdgeStreamDeliveryRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principal edgestream.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-edge-archive/distributions/* and nothing else. Keep the existing bucket policy exactly as it is, since the role's own policy supplies the write permission. In the EdgeStream console, select the distribution, choose cdn-edge-archive as the destination, and supply the role ARN. EdgeStream assumes the role once per hour and uploads one gzip file per edge location under distributions/DISTRIBUTION_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/. Every record in these files contains the request time, edge location code, requested path, response status, and cache result. Confirm delivery by checking that files for the previous hour exist under the distribution's prefix.

This guide enables EdgeStream to write hourly edge request logs for a content distribution into the bucket cdn-edge-archive. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the EdgeStream service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that names the principal edgestream.example.com as the allowed principal. Set that statement to allow PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-edge-archive/distributions/* and nothing else. Do not create a role for EdgeStream, since the bucket policy supplies the write permission by itself. In the EdgeStream console, select the distribution, choose cdn-edge-archive as the destination, and leave the role setting blank. EdgeStream calls the storage service as its service principal once per hour and uploads one gzip file per edge location under distributions/DISTRIBUTION_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/. Every record in these files contains the request time, edge location code, requested path, response status, and cache result. Confirm delivery by checking that files for the previous hour exist under the distribution's prefix.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper to deliver JSON audit events from account 111122223333 to the bucket sec-audit-store, which is owned by the same account. Access is granted only through an IAM role that TrailKeeper assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named TrailKeeperWriterRole and add a trust policy that lets the service principal trailkeeper.example.com assume it. Give the role an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::sec-audit-store/trail/AWSLogs-111122223333/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::sec-audit-store. The bucket policy of sec-audit-store stays as it is and does not mention TrailKeeper. In the TrailKeeper trail settings, enter the bucket name, the prefix trail/, and the ARN of the role. TrailKeeper assumes the role every fifteen minutes and writes gzip-compressed JSON files under trail/AWSLogs-111122223333/YYYY/MM/DD/. Each file lists API calls with the caller identity, source address, operation name, target resource, and result. Check delivery by opening the trail status page, which reports the time of the last successful write.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper to deliver JSON audit events from account 111122223333 to the bucket sec-audit-store, which is owned by the same account. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the TrailKeeper service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the principal trailkeeper.example.com. Allow PutObject on arn:example:storage:::sec-audit-store/trail/AWSLogs-111122223333/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::sec-audit-store in that statement. No role or identity-based policy is part of this setup, so the bucket policy is the only place where permissions are defined. In the TrailKeeper trail settings, enter the bucket name and the prefix trail/, and leave the role field unset. TrailKeeper writes as its service principal every fifteen minutes and stores gzip-compressed JSON files under trail/AWSLogs-111122223333/YYYY/MM/DD/. Each file lists API calls with the caller identity, source address, operation name, target resource, and result. Check delivery by opening the trail status page, which reports the time of the last successful write.

This guide configures QueryLedger to export slow query logs from a managed database instance to the bucket db-slowlog-export once per day. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the QueryLedger export service assumes, and the bucket policy remains unchanged. Create a role named QueryLedgerExportRole whose trust policy permits the service principal queryledger.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/instances/*. The bucket has versioning enabled, and the existing bucket policy does not need an additional statement for this export. In the instance's logging settings, specify the bucket, the prefix instances/, and the role ARN. At 02:00 UTC the service assumes the role and uploads the rotated log as instances/INSTANCE_ID/YYYY-MM-DD.log.gz. Each entry records the statement text, execution time, rows examined, and the database user. Verify the export by listing the instance's prefix the next morning and confirming that a new object version exists.

This guide configures QueryLedger to export slow query logs from a managed database instance to the bucket db-slowlog-export once per day. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the QueryLedger service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy that names queryledger.example.com as the principal. Let that statement allow PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/instances/*. The bucket has versioning enabled, and no role or identity-based policy is needed because the bucket policy carries the permissions. In the instance's logging settings, specify the bucket and the prefix instances/, and leave the role field empty. At 02:00 UTC the service writes as its service principal and uploads the rotated log as instances/INSTANCE_ID/YYYY-MM-DD.log.gz. Each entry records the statement text, execution time, rows examined, and the database user. Verify the export by listing the instance's prefix the next morning and confirming that a new object version exists.

This guide allows NetFlowRecorder to publish network flow logs for virtual network vnet-prod-01 to the bucket netflow-records in 10-minute batches. Access is granted only through an IAM role that NetFlowRecorder assumes, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a role named NetFlowRecorderRole with a trust policy that names netflowrecorder.example.com as the service allowed to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow PutObject on arn:example:storage:::netflow-records/flows/vnet-prod-01/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Do not edit the bucket policy of netflow-records, since all permissions come from the role's policy. In the flow log configuration, select vnet-prod-01, set the destination bucket and the prefix flows/vnet-prod-01/, and enter the role ARN. After each aggregation window the service assumes the role and writes a plain-text file named WINDOW_START_UTC.log.gz under that prefix. Each line contains source and destination addresses, ports, protocol, packet count, byte count, and an accept or reject flag. Verify the configuration by generating test traffic and finding its records in the next batch.

This guide configures PodTrace to ship container cluster logs to the bucket cluster-logs-short, which expires objects after 30 days through a lifecycle rule. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the PodTrace collector service assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named PodTraceShipperRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principalpodtrace.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cluster-logs-short/clusters/* and ListBucket on the bucket. The bucket policy and the lifecycle rule are left exactly as they are. In the cluster's logging settings, enter the bucket, the prefix clusters/, and the role ARN. The collector assumes the role every five minutes and uploads newline-delimited JSON files to clusters/CLUSTER_NAME/NAMESPACE/YYYY/MM/DD/. Each line holds the pod name, container name, stream type, timestamp, and message text. Verify the setup by restarting a test pod and confirming that its output appears in the next uploaded file.

This guide configures GatewayScribe to deliver API request logs for the stage payments-prod to the bucket api-req-logs in Parquet format. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the GatewayScribe delivery service assumes, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named GatewayScribeDeliveryRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal gatewayscribe.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::api-req-logs/gateway/payments-prod/* and nothing outside that prefix. Keep the bucket policy of api-req-logs unchanged, because the role's policy defines the permission. In the stage's log settings, enter the bucket, the prefix gateway/payments-prod/, the format Parquet, and the role ARN. Every hour the service assumes the role and writes one file per partition to gateway/payments-prod/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/. Each row includes the request ID, method, route, response code, latency in milliseconds, and client address. Verify the setup by calling the stage once and querying the newest partition for that request ID.

This guide enables ResolverLog to deliver DNS query logs from the resolver endpoint rs-east-02 to the bucket dns-query-logs, which is located in a different region than the resolver. Access is granted only through an IAM role that the ResolverLog service assumes, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Create a role named ResolverLogWriterRole with a trust policy that lets the service principal resolverlog.example.com assume it. Add an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/resolver/rs-east-02/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The bucket policy does not need any new statement, since the role carries the write permission across regions. In the resolver's logging configuration, specify the bucket, the prefix resolver/rs-east-02/, and the role ARN. Each minute the service assumes the role and uploads a newline-delimited JSON file named by its start timestamp. Each record shows the queried name, record type, response code, client subnet, and query time. Verify the configuration by issuing a test query and finding the name in the file for that minute.
